note: Every source below was opened and read during this session. 'verifies' lists the exact claim it supports. Rows marked official:'secondary' are cited only for arithmetically-derived cross-checks and never carry a model input on their own.

sources.title: Proposition 19 — intergenerational transfer exclusion (landing page, comparison charts, Letters to Assessors index)
sources.verifies: Prop 19 replaced Prop 58/193 on 2021-02-16; principal residence + one-year occupancy; value limit = FBYV + $1M; claim deadlines; RTC 63.2 implementing statute

sources.title: LTA No. 2026/026 — Proposition 19 Intergenerational Transfer Exclusion FAQ
sources.verifies: Family home definition; no exceptions to the one-year occupancy rule; multi-unit buildings (only the occupied unit qualifies); trusts are looked through; LLCs disqualify; long-term leases excluded; prospective relief; filing deadlines

sources.title: LTA No. 2025/009 — Intergenerational Transfer Exclusion, adjustment of the $1 million amount
sources.verifies: $1,044,586 cushion for transfers 2025-02-16 through 2027-02-15; $1,022,600 for 2023-2025; $1,000,000 for 2021-2023; biennial FHFA-HPI adjustment

sources.title: LTA No. 2026/002 — 2026-27 California Consumer Price Index inflation factor
sources.verifies: 2026-27 assessment roll inflation factor = 1.02 (CCPI +3.307%, capped at 2%); full historical factor table back to 1976-77

sources.title: Revenue & Taxation Code §63.2 — intergenerational transfer exclusion (statute text)
sources.verifies: Statutory text of the exclusion: principal-residence requirement, homeowners'-exemption filing, exclusion removal on move-out, new taxable value formula, legal-entity carve-out

sources.title: Revenue & Taxation Code §11911 — Documentary Transfer Tax Act
sources.verifies: County transfer tax of $0.55 per $500 (0.11%) and the city half-rate authorization

sources.title: Civil Code §1947.12 — Tenant Protection Act (AB 1482) rent cap
sources.verifies: Statewide cap of 5% + cost-of-living change, never more than 10% in 12 months; exemptions incl. housing with a certificate of occupancy in the previous 15 years

sources.title: Estate tax — filing threshold by year of death
sources.verifies: 2025 filing threshold $13,990,000; 2026 threshold $15,000,000; Form 706 requirement; portability election mechanics

sources.title: What's new — Estate and gift tax (P.L. 119-21 / OBBBA)
sources.verifies: OBBBA (signed 2025-07-04, P.L. 119-21) raised IRC §2010(c)(3) basic exclusion to $15,000,000 for 2026

sources.title: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 — 2026 inflation adjustments
sources.verifies: 2026 annual gift exclusion $19,000 (§4.42); non-citizen-spouse gift exclusion $194,000; §2032A special-use valuation cap $1,460,000 (§4.41); 2026 capital-gain breakpoints (§4.03); 2026 brackets (§4.01)

sources.title: 26 U.S.C. §1014 — basis of property acquired from a decedent
sources.verifies: Stepped-up basis = fair market value at date of death; basis rules for property passing from a decedent, including trusts

sources.title: Topic No. 701 — Sale of your home (§121 exclusion)
sources.verifies: $250,000 / $500,000 gain exclusion on a principal residence; ownership and use tests (2 of last 5 years)

sources.title: Publication 523 (2025), Selling Your Home
sources.verifies: Exclusion worksheets and eligibility detail; OBBBA termination of residential clean-energy credits after 2025

sources.title: Publication 527 (2025), Residential Rental Property
sources.verifies: Rental income/expense treatment, basis of property changed to rental use, depreciation, personal-use limits

sources.title: Retirement topics — Required minimum distributions
sources.verifies: RMD age 73; beneficiary distribution rules; 25%/10% excise tax for missed RMDs

sources.title: Bill analysis, SB 378 (2019-20) — California Estate & Gift Taxes, estate 'pick-up' tax
sources.verifies: California does not conform to federal estate/GST tax; the state 'pick-up' tax equals a federal credit repealed after 2004, therefore zero

sources.title: 2025 Form 593 — Real Estate Withholding Statement
sources.verifies: 3⅓% withholding on California real-property sales; full-exemption certifications (IRC §121 principal residence, zero gain, decedent's last residence, 1031)

sources.title: 2024 Form FTB 3840 — California Like-Kind Exchanges
sources.verifies: Annual reporting of California-source deferred gain on out-of-state 1031 replacement property (the 'clawback' tracking form)

sources.title: 2025 California Tax Rate Schedules (Form 540)
sources.verifies: California PIT brackets: 1%–12.3%, with the 1% Behavioral Health Services surcharge above $1M producing the 13.3% top rate; standard deduction amounts
